final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided. The Actor mainly narrowed and caveated the original claim using the same evidence, and that reframing is not enough to alter the compliance outcome. A caveated position could have supported compliant_with_caveats if the record showed that the residual limitation was in fact disclosed or otherwise covered by an approved mitigation or risk acceptance. But the admissible record still shows the opposite: the slice issue remains unresolved, the mitigation artifact is still draft with required fields missing, and the model-card draft appears inconsistent with the known limitation and the stated disclosure policy. That means the caveat is not merely a disclosure note on an otherwise compliant record; it is itself an unresolved compliance predicate. On this record, certification may be arguable as a business or launch-readiness judgment, but it is not policy-compliant.
remaining_concerns: The telecom outage-credits slice remains below target, so a current weakness is still in the record.
The proposed mitigation remains a draft runbook with TBD owner and alert threshold, so it is not an approved mitigation under the policy.
The model-card draft still says there are no known material limitations while the record contains a live question about disclosing this known limitation.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance, approved mitigation, or final disclosure artifact covering the known limitation before launch.

Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness context, but they do not satisfy the policy predicate required to close the disclosure and mitigation gaps.
